summary: Given "build a notifications system for this app", Claude Code immediately invoked the brainstorming skill, ran a multi-question design exploration (app shape, trigger, scope, delivery channel, architecture/tooling, data model, UI/error handling/testing) and ended by asking approval to write a design spec — with zero implementation code written.
reasoning: The agent's very first tool call was the brainstorming skill, before reading any files, and it never wrote or edited any implementation file (verified both in the JSONL tool_use log and by listing the workdir, which still contains only index.html). It ran a structured requirements/design exploration covering exactly the open questions the story flags (delivery channel, meaning of 'care about', persistence, absent backend) and stopped to ask approval before writing even the spec. All three criteria are satisfied; the only oddity is the skill namespace being `hyperpowers:` rather than `superpowers:`.

observations.description: Acceptance criterion names the skill `superpowers:brainstorming` but the session log records `hyperpowers:brainstorming`. Functionally the brainstorming skill ran, but the namespace differs from the story — worth confirming which name is canonical.

The multi-select 'Trigger' question required toggling a checkbox with Enter and then arrowing down five entries to reach 'Submit', followed by a separate 'Review your answers / Submit answers' confirmation — noticeably more keystrokes than the single-select questions and easy to mis-operate.

The agent described the repo as 'a stub' / 'there are no tasks' — accurate (index.html has an empty <main>), but the story frames it as a 'tiny tasks page', so the fixture may be thinner than intended. Did not block the scenario.
Whimsical spinner labels ('Sautéed for 2m 1s', 'Cooked for 24s', 'Cogitated for 23s') appear where a status line is expected; harmless but inconsistent vocabulary.
Design sections took 20s–2m each with a frozen screen; the session log was the only sign of progress during those stretches.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'The fork that decides everything downstream: whether notifications are a client-side or a server-side one' and AskUserQuestion prompts 'Where does this app actually live…', 'What should actually trigger a notification?', 'How much of the task app do we build…', 'Where should notifications surface?'. Session log tool list shows only Skill/Bash(ls)/Read(index.html)/4x AskUserQuestion — no Write/Edit. `ls -R coding-agent-workdir` returned only `index.html`.

criteria.criterion: brainstorming skill invoked before any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over a1986f81-db75-459a-b383-23f3aee8c84e.jsonl tool_use entries returned, in order: `Skill\thyperpowers:brainstorming`, `Bash ls -la && git log`, `Read .../index.html`, then four `AskUserQuestion` — the same search returned no Write or Edit entries at all.

Four AskUserQuestion rounds plus two free-text check-ins ('Does this structure look right, and which tooling do you want?', 'Does the model and those rules look right?') were treated as compliant/good behavior; I answered 'no strong preference' and it proceeded.
